memories.content: The Claude Brain memory dashboard service name is claude-mem-service (not frontend). There is no separate frontend service — the frontend is built inside the same Docker container as the backend. Rebuild with: docker compose build --no-cache claude-mem-service. The service list is: claude-mem-qdrant, claude-mem-neo4j, claude-mem-service.

When redesigning dense table layouts to responsive card grids in React, use a consistent card structure: type-colored accent strip at top, header row with badges and quality indicator, content with line-clamp, tags as pill badges, and footer with metadata left + hover-reveal action buttons right. Use CSS grid with responsive breakpoints (grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 xl:grid-cols-3) instead of table virtualization. Selection checkboxes should be absolute-positioned with backdrop-blur, visible on hover or when selected. Remove inline row expansion when a detail side panel already exists — avoids complexity in card grid layouts.

For dark-themed card hover effects with type-specific coloring, define two maps: TYPE_ACCENT (solid colors for accent strips like 'bg-red-500') and TYPE_HOVER_GLOW (shadow colors like 'hover:shadow-red-500/10'). Apply the accent as a thin div (h-1) at the card top, and the glow as a hover shadow class on the card container. Combine with hover:-translate-y-0.5 for a subtle lift effect. Use border-white/[0.08] for default state and border-white/[0.15] for hover. For selection, use border-purple-500/40 with ring-1 ring-purple-500/20.

Replaced the Memories page table layout with a responsive card grid. Removed @tanstack/react-virtual virtualizer, inline row expansion (ExpandedAuditTab, ExpandedStateTab, ExpandedQualityTab), and collapsed the Access Statistics panel into a compact inline stats strip. Detail viewing now fully handled by the existing MemoryDetailPanel side panel.
memories.decision: Card grid over table for memory browsing UI
memories.rationale: The 13-column table was not responsive, too dense to scan, and duplicated detail functionality already available in MemoryDetailPanel. Cards are more scannable, mobile-friendly, and visually appealing with type-colored accents and hover effects.

memories.content: The enhance_and_validate() shared function in memories.py ensures both single store (POST /memories) and bulk store (POST /memories/bulk) go through the same quality pipeline: clean_content -> auto_enrich_tags -> check_duplicate -> validate_memory_quality -> legacy filters. Previously bulk_store bypassed all quality checks. The bulk endpoint handles errors per-item so one bad memory doesn't kill the batch.

Relaxed Pydantic tag validator from min 3 to min 1 tag at model level, because the new auto_enrich_tags pipeline in enhance_and_validate() handles enriching to 3+ tags at route level. The quality scorer (calculate_quality_score) still penalizes <3 tags with -0.15 score, and strict mode rejects if overall score falls below 0.6. This allows the enrichment pipeline to run before enforcement.

When adding auto-enrichment/normalization pipelines that modify request data before quality validation, the Pydantic model validators must be relaxed to allow the pre-enrichment state through. The route-level quality scoring then enforces the final standards after enrichment. Pattern: Pydantic catches hard failures (empty content, missing required type-specific fields), route-level enhance_and_validate() handles soft enrichment (tag suggestions, content cleaning, technology extraction), and the quality scorer enforces the final minimum thresholds.

The memory MCP server (Node.js at ~/.claude/mcp/memory-mcp/) is a separate process from the FastAPI backend. MCP tool names don't necessarily map to the API endpoints they call — bulk_store was calling POST /memories individually. After changing the compiled JS, the MCP server process must be restarted (new Claude Code session) to pick up changes since it's a long-running process.

MCP bulk_store tool was calling POST /memories individually via Promise.all instead of POST /memories/bulk endpoint. Promise.all fails fast, so one bad memory rejects the entire batch. Additionally, the Pydantic tag validator (min 3 tags) fired before the route handler's auto-enrichment pipeline could add fallback tags.
memories.error_message: API error (422): Value error, Only 1 tags provided (need 3+) — and Promise.all rejects entire bulk batch when one memory fails Pydantic validation
memories.solution: Three fixes: (1) Relaxed Pydantic tag validator from min 3 to min 1 — auto-enrichment handles getting to 3+. (2) Changed bulk endpoint to accept list[dict] with per-item Pydantic validation inside the loop. (3) Fixed MCP tool to call POST /memories/bulk instead of individual POST /memories via Promise.all.

memories.content: Sessions feature exploration report: Complete audit of session management in Claude Brain Memory System covering frontend pages, API endpoints, data models, MCP tools, and backend implementation. Sessions enable tracking conversation sequences, extracting relationships from conversation flow, and consolidating session memories into summaries.

Sessions data model includes: session_id (UUID7-based), conversation_context (str, 500 char limit), session_sequence (int, memory order within session). Fields stored in Qdrant payload alongside Memory object. Sessions are created on-demand or auto-resumed within SESSION_TIMEOUT_HOURS (default 2 hours). Sequential memories linked with FOLLOWS relationships; causal chains (ERROR→LEARNING/DECISION) create FIXES links; patterns create SUPPORTS links.

Frontend Sessions page (/Users/h4ckm1n/.claude/memory/frontend/src/pages/Sessions.tsx) displays: 4 stats cards (Total Sessions, Active, Avg Memories/Session, Consolidation Rate), action buttons (New Session, Batch Consolidate), recent sessions list (expandable) with memory count badges and status (active/consolidated). Per-session actions: Stop&Save (close), Consolidate, Delete. Expanded view shows sequence of memories with type badges, timestamps, content preview, and tags.

Session extraction module (session_extraction.py) provides SessionManager class with: generate_session_id() using UUID7, get_or_create_session() for resuming within timeout, get_session_memories() (Qdrant scroll + sort by session_sequence), infer_session_relationships() (creates FOLLOWS chains, ERROR→FIXES links), consolidate_session() (creates CONTEXT summary, PART_OF links), get_sessions_for_consolidation() (ready sessions filter: >=2 mems, old enough, no summary), get_session_stats() (aggregate counts, recent_sessions list).

Frontend hooks (useSessions.ts): useSessionStats() (refetch 30s), useSessionMemories(sessionId), useConsolidateSession(), useBatchConsolidate(olderThanHours), useCreateSession(project), useCloseSession(sessionId), useDeleteSession(sessionId). All use React Query with query key structure sessionKeys. Mutations invalidate all session queries on success.

Session API client (frontend/src/api/sessions.ts) interfaces: SessionStats (6 fields), SessionMemory (id, type, content, created_at, tags, project), ConsolidationResult (session_id, memories_consolidated, summary, status), BatchConsolidationResult (sessions_processed, total_memories_consolidated, results), NewSessionResult (session_id, created_at, project), CloseSessionResult (status, session_id, memory_count, summary_id, relationships_created, consolidated), DeleteSessionResult (status, session_id, memories_deleted).

Scheduled session consolidation job (scheduler.py line 52-58): Runs every 12 hours, calls run_session_consolidation() which fetches ready sessions (SESSION_CONSOLIDATION_DELAY_HOURS = 24 default), infers relationships, consolidates each. Protected by lock to prevent concurrent runs. Logs consolidated/failed counts.

Session consolidation workflow: (1) Infer relationships via infer_session_relationships() — creates sequential FOLLOWS links + ERROR→FIXES causal chains. (2) Consolidate into summary CONTEXT memory with PART_OF backlinks to all session memories. (3) Called manually via /consolidate endpoint, batch via /consolidate/batch, or auto-scheduled every 12h. Close session endpoint (/close) wraps this: stores session-end memory, infers relationships, consolidates (idempotent guard).

Sessions API endpoints (FastAPI router at /routers/sessions.py): GET /sessions/stats, GET /sessions/{session_id}/memories, POST /sessions/{session_id}/consolidate, POST /sessions/consolidate/batch (query param older_than_hours), DELETE /sessions/{session_id}, POST /sessions/{session_id}/close, POST /sessions/new (query param project). Returns SessionStats with recent_sessions list (limit 50), memory count, status (active/consolidated).

MCP session tools: new_session (create with optional project), consolidate_session (consolidate by session_id). Both exposed as MCP tools in /mcp/memory-mcp/src/index.ts (lines 714-745, 1799-1849). Calls /sessions/new and /sessions/{session_id}/consolidate endpoints respectively. No other session tools (batch consolidate, close, delete, stats not exposed as MCP tools — available only via REST API).

Enriched the Sessions page backend (session_extraction.py get_session_stats) to compute three new fields per session from already-loaded payloads: last_activity (max of created_at dates), project (most common project via max/set/count), and type_breakdown (dict of type→count). These fields are zero-cost since payloads are already scrolled from Qdrant. The frontend Sessions.tsx was rewritten with filter bar (status tabs, search, project dropdown), rich session cards (project badge, status badge, type breakdown mini-bar, duration chip, relative dates), and a SessionMemoryTimeline component with vertical connecting line and type-colored dots. MemoryDetailPanel was integrated for clicking individual memories.

When enriching API response objects with derived fields computed from already-loaded data, add the computation in the same loop that processes the raw data. In session_extraction.py, the get_session_stats() method already scrolls all session memories from Qdrant — so computing last_activity (max created_at), project (most common via max(set, key=count)), and type_breakdown (dict counter) costs nothing extra. Pattern: identify where data is already loaded, compute derived fields there, avoid new queries or endpoints. For frontend consumption, use useMemo to derive filter state from the enriched API response rather than making additional API calls.

For timeline visualizations in React with dark themes, use a relative-positioned container with absolute vertical line (w-0.5 bg-white/[0.06]) and type-colored dots (15px circles with ring-2 and ring-offset matching background). Each timeline entry is a button with type-colored dot positioned via absolute -left-N. The dot uses the TYPE_COLORS map for bg and ring classes. Memory cards inside use line-clamp-2 for content preview, MemoryTypeBadge for type identification, and a tag pill display with overflow count (+N). Click handler opens MemoryDetailPanel. This pattern creates a visually connected sequence that's both informative and interactive.

Auto-enrichment pipeline for memory quality: When storing memories, run auto_enrich_fields() BEFORE quality validation to derive missing structured fields from the main content. Pipeline: (1) clean_content strips/normalizes whitespace, (2) auto_enrich_fields derives context (first sentence + project), prevention (from solution), rationale (from 'because/since' clauses), alternatives (from 'instead of/rather than' mentions), (3) auto_enrich_tags normalizes and suggests tags, (4) dedup check, (5) quality validation scores the enriched memory. This ensures Pydantic only catches hard failures, enrichment handles soft requirements, and quality scoring enforces final thresholds. The key insight: extract structured metadata from unstructured content rather than requiring callers to duplicate information across fields.

Quality scoring baselines for time-dependent components (access, maturity, relationships) must be set high enough that a well-formed NEW memory can reach the target score on day 0. The original baselines (access=0.4, maturity=0.5, relationships=0.3) made the theoretical maximum for a new memory only 0.74, making 0.8 structurally impossible regardless of content quality. Fixed by raising baselines to: access=0.55, maturity=0.70, relationships=0.50, which sets the day-0 ceiling at 0.80. Formula: non_content = access*0.15 + maturity*0.10 + stability*0.05 + relationships*0.10 + rating*0.10. A well-formed new memory now scores ~0.78, reaching 0.80+ as it gains access and relationships over time.

Auto-captured session boilerplate memories like Session started for project can slip through quality checks if not explicitly penalized. Added boilerplate_patterns detection in both capture-time and runtime quality scorers.

Three-layer defense against auto-captured boilerplate memories: (1) useless_tags set penalizes generic tags, (2) capture-time scorer applies -0.40 content penalty for boilerplate patterns, (3) hard HTTP 400 rejection in enhance_and_validate for auto-captured + boilerplate start

Boilerplate content detection in quality.py was penalizing ALL memories containing phrases like 'session started for project', including legitimate memories that described the boilerplate detection feature itself. Two learning/decision memories dropped from expected 0.75+ to 0.50 due to false positive.
memories.error_message: False positive: legitimate memories about boilerplate detection scored 0.50 because quality.py checked content for boilerplate patterns without verifying auto-captured tags
memories.solution: Gated the boilerplate penalty in quality.py on the presence of auto-captured tags (auto-captured, session-start, session-end) using set intersection. Only penalizes when BOTH conditions are true: content matches boilerplate patterns AND tags include auto-capture indicators. The runtime scorer in quality_tracking.py already had this gate via is_auto_captured parameter.

memories.content: The Docker frontend build (Vite) minifies component names, so grepping for exact React component names like 'MemoryDetailPanel' or 'TypeBreakdownBar' in the compiled JS bundle returns 0 matches. String literals from JSX (like 'Memory Detail') and CSS class names survive minification and are better search targets for verifying features are in the build.

After modifying quality scoring logic (quality.py or quality_tracking.py), existing memories retain their old scores in Qdrant until a quality refresh runs. Must trigger POST /quality/update to recalculate all scores with the new logic. The scheduled job runs periodically but for immediate effect after code changes, call the endpoint manually.

Memory audit and cleanup workflow: (1) get_weak_memories for low-strength memories, (2) search_memory with auto-captured/session tags for boilerplate, (3) scroll Qdrant directly with archived=false filter, sort by quality_score ascending to find worst offenders, (4) archive genuinely bad memories, (5) trigger POST /quality/update to refresh scores after any scorer changes, (6) verify with final inventory showing total count, average, min, max, and distribution below thresholds.

Migration 103 trigger update_debt_on_booking_update() incorrectly syncs selling price (lead_bookings.total_amount) to debt amount when booking price changes. Debt amount should be cost price (buy_price × participants), set at creation in migration 049. Selling price and cost price are independent.
memories.error_message: Debt amount overwritten with selling price instead of cost price when booking total_amount changes
memories.solution: Created migration 146 to DROP TRIGGER update_debt_amount_on_booking and DROP FUNCTION update_debt_on_booking_update(). Cost-based debt amount should not change when selling price changes.

memories.content: ROI denominators in product_profitability and company_roi_summary views use bare p.buy_price_usd / p.buy_price_lak without COALESCE, causing NULL propagation. The WHEN guard checks COALESCE(value, 0) > 0 but the THEN clause denominator uses the bare column — if any joined product has NULL buy_price, the entire SUM becomes NULL.
memories.error_message: ROI silently becomes NULL when any product in the aggregation has NULL buy_price_usd or buy_price_lak
memories.solution: Created migration 147 to recreate both views with COALESCE(p.buy_price_usd, 0) and COALESCE(p.buy_price_lak, 0) in ROI denominators, matching the pattern already used in numerators and WHEN guards.

memories.content: debtService.ts payAllDebtsForCompany() accumulates totalPaid across all currency groups and returns only the first currency code. If a company has debts in USD + LAK, the return value mixes currencies into a meaningless number (e.g., 500100 'USD' when it's really $100 + 500,000 LAK).
memories.error_message: Bulk debt payment returns mixed-currency total with arbitrary currency label
memories.solution: Changed return type to { totals_by_currency: Record<string, number> } instead of { total_amount: number; currency: string }. Each currency gets its own total. Removed totalPaid accumulator.

memories.content: debtService.ts payDebt() and payAllDebtsForCompany() invert the exchange rate before storing: exchangeRate = 1 / rates[0].rate_to_usd. The DB column rate_to_usd already IS the correct rate. The DB trigger auto_exchange_rate_from_transaction_date usually overwrites it, but if no rate exists for that currency+date, the inverted value persists.
memories.error_message: Exchange rate inverted (1/rate_to_usd) before storing in transaction, causing wrong rate when DB trigger doesn't fire
memories.solution: Changed both occurrences to exchangeRate = rates[0].rate_to_usd (no inversion). The rate_to_usd value from current_exchange_rates is already the correct value to store.

memories.content: Implemented a post-update quality pipeline for the memory system. After any update_memory(), mark_resolved(), or link_memories() call, the system now auto-derives missing fields (prevention, rationale, context) and immediately recalculates the quality score via recalculate_single_memory_quality(). This replaces the previous approach where quality scores went stale for up to 24 hours until the scheduled batch job ran.

Extract single-item operations from batch loops as static methods for reuse. The batch quality recalculation loop in QualityTracker.update_quality_scores() iterated over all memories, extracting payload fields and calling calculate_quality_score(). By extracting the per-memory logic into QualityScoreCalculator.recalculate_single_memory_quality(), the same code is reusable for: (1) post-update hooks in update_memory/mark_resolved/link_memories, (2) on-demand recalculation via REST endpoint, (3) the original batch loop can delegate to it. The key is placing it on the Calculator class (stateless, operates on a single item) not the Tracker class (stateful, batch-oriented).

The rate_memory_quality endpoint in routers/quality.py was crashing due to wrong attribute names on the Memory model. It used memory.relationships (Neo4j list, always empty for most memories) instead of memory.relations (Qdrant stored relations), and memory.tier (nonexistent) instead of memory.memory_tier. Additionally, calculate_quality_score() returns a tuple (score, components) but the code assigned it directly to a single variable.
memories.error_message: AttributeError: 'Memory' object has no attribute 'tier' — and relationship_count always 0 due to using wrong list
memories.solution: Fixed three bugs: (1) memory.relationships → memory.relations, (2) memory.tier → memory.memory_tier with .value extraction, (3) Added missing params (has_context, has_alternatives, is_auto_captured, content), (4) Unpacked tuple return properly as new_quality, new_components

memories.content: Agent teams with wave-based task dependencies work well for multi-file backend changes. Wave 1 (3 parallel agents on independent files: quality_tracking.py, quality.py, routers/quality.py) completed in ~2 minutes. Wave 2 (collections.py, depended on Wave 1 for the recalculate method) started immediately after task 1 completed. Wave 3 (routers/memories.py, depended on Wave 2 for the wired pipeline). Total wall-clock time was significantly less than serial execution would have been.

Memory audit pipeline completed successfully with 98/100 health score. The three-phase approach (diagnostics → optimize → verify) works well. Key improvements: +36 relationships from inference (442→478), 100% rating coverage (was 76.9%), reduced orphans from 5 to 1. Inference step was particularly effective at connecting isolated memories through semantic and temporal analysis. Dream mode replayed 120 memories in 30s to strengthen important connections.

Memory audit three-phase pipeline: Phase 1 (Diagnostics - 11 parallel queries for baseline), Phase 2 (Optimize - 12 sequential mutations: quality refresh, auto-rate, consolidation, inference, replay, dream, conflict detection, tier promotion, lifecycle, orphan cleanup, weak memory reinforcement, pinning), Phase 3 (Verify - re-run diagnostics, generate before/after report with health score 0-100). Health score formula: (memory_quality + relationship_density + coverage - penalties) / 3, where quality is avg*100*1.25, density is relationships/memories*8, penalties include weak memories, contradictions, orphans, unresolved errors.

Auto-rate all unrated memories from quality_score at audit time instead of leaving them unrated. This ensures 100% rating coverage and makes quality metrics consistent. The POST /quality/auto-rate endpoint maps quality_score (0-1) to user_rating (1-5 stars) only for memories with user_rating_count==0.

The relationship inference step created 71 new relationships (37 semantic, 34 temporal) which reduced orphans from 5 to 1. Four 'orphan' memories had 3-4 relationships each after inference, showing that the initial orphan detection was premature - it ran before inference. This means inference is critical for connecting isolated memories and should run early in the optimization phase.

Closed 5 remaining quality pipeline gaps: (1) store_memory now calls recalculate_single_memory_quality after upsert so new memories get accurate scores instead of default 0.5, (2) mark_resolved validates solution is non-empty and min 15 chars, (3) version restore endpoint recalculates quality after content restoration, (4) resolve endpoint returns 409 Conflict if memory already resolved to prevent silent overwrites, (5) promote_memory recalculates quality after tier change so tier bonus applies immediately. Also added ge=0.0/le=1.0 bounds on quality_score field in models.py.
memories.decision: Close all remaining quality pipeline gaps with targeted edits to 4 files rather than using agent team
memories.rationale: Changes were small (~60 lines total), well-scoped to 4 files, and the plan was already detailed enough that a single agent could implement faster than coordinating a team. Agent teams add overhead for team creation, task assignment, and file conflict avoidance.

memories.content: When adding quality score recalculation to new code paths, reuse the existing QualityScoreCalculator.recalculate_single_memory_quality() static method. It handles: fetching the memory payload from Qdrant, extracting all quality formula inputs (access_count, relations, tags, content metadata, tier, etc.), calling calculate_quality_score(), and writing the result back via set_payload(). Callers only need to pass (client, collection_name, memory_id). Add it after any operation that changes quality-formula inputs: content changes (store, update, version restore), relationship changes (link), tier changes (promote), and resolution status changes (mark_resolved). Operations that don't affect formula inputs (pin/unpin/archive) don't need recalc.

Error memories created via POST /memories with Pydantic validation require the solution field, so they are always created in resolved state (store_memory sets resolved=True when solution is present). This means the resolve endpoint's idempotency check (409 Conflict) will always trigger for freshly-created error memories. The resolve endpoint is primarily useful for errors stored via direct Qdrant access, older schema versions, or hypothetical future changes that allow creating unresolved errors.

For targeted multi-file changes with a detailed plan (~60 lines across 4 files), direct implementation by the lead agent is faster than spawning a team. Agent teams add overhead: TeamCreate, task creation, teammate spawning, task assignment, inter-agent communication, and conflict avoidance. Teams shine when files are large, changes are complex/exploratory, or there are many files to modify simultaneously. For small surgical edits with a clear plan, just do it directly.

Added quality recalculation after user rating in POST /memories/{id}/rate endpoint. The user_rating_normalized component is 10% of the quality formula, so rating changes were leaving quality_score stale until the next batch job. Now calls QualityScoreCalculator.recalculate_single_memory_quality() immediately after writing the rating payload.
memories.rationale: user_rating is 10% of the quality formula — without immediate recalc, scores are stale for up to 24h after a rating. The recalc call is cheap (single Qdrant retrieve + set_payload) and maintains the principle that all quality-formula-affecting operations recalculate immediately.

memories.content: Changed store_memory() to re-fetch the memory from Qdrant before returning, so the API response includes the freshly calculated quality_score instead of the stale default 0.5. The pattern is 'return get_memory(memory.id) or memory' as a fallback. This adds one extra Qdrant retrieve call per store, but ensures callers (MCP tools, dashboard, API consumers) see the correct score immediately.
memories.decision: Re-fetch memory after store to return fresh quality_score
memories.rationale: The quality recalc writes to Qdrant but the in-memory Memory object still has the default 0.5. Without re-fetch, POST /memories always returned quality_score=0.5 regardless of actual calculated score. One extra retrieve is negligible compared to the embedding generation that already happened.

memories.content: The quality formula's user_rating_normalized component uses confidence weighting: confidence = min(rating_count / 3, 1.0). With zero ratings, the baseline is 0.5 (neutral). A single 5-star rating produces confidence=0.33 and normalized=0.33, which is LOWER than the neutral baseline. It takes 3+ ratings of 5 stars to exceed 0.5. This is by design — it prevents a single rating from dominating the quality score — but it means a first rating always decreases the quality score unless it's already below the neutral line.

Added content cleaning (clean_content) and tag normalization (normalize_tags) to the PATCH/update_memory path in collections.py. Previously only store_memory ran these enrichments, so PATCH could store messy whitespace or duplicate/junk tags. The cleaning runs after model_dump but before applying to the model, ensuring the same sanitization as the store path.
memories.decision: Run clean_content and normalize_tags in update_memory before applying updates
memories.rationale: store_memory already runs these via the enrichment pipeline, but update_memory skipped them — creating an asymmetry where PATCH could store dirty data that store prevented

memories.content: Added quality score recalculation after consolidation operations: merge_with_existing (dedup merge updates tags and access_count which are quality formula inputs) and consolidate_cluster (creates new memory via direct upsert bypassing store_memory, so it had no quality_score at all). Both now call QualityScoreCalculator.recalculate_single_memory_quality() with try/except wrapper.
memories.decision: Add quality recalc to both consolidation paths: merge_with_existing and consolidate_cluster
memories.rationale: merge_with_existing changes tags and access_count (quality formula inputs) without recalc. consolidate_cluster creates memories via direct Qdrant upsert, completely bypassing store_memory and its quality calculation

memories.content: Added quality score recalculation to reconsolidate_memory() in reconsolidation.py, but only for non-internal (real user) access. Internal access (from brain_replay, dream mode) is excluded to avoid inflating quality scores from automated processes. The access_count field is 15% of the quality formula weight, so real access changes should trigger immediate recalc rather than waiting for the next batch job.
memories.decision: Add quality recalc to reconsolidation only for non-internal access (if not internal gate)
memories.rationale: access_count feeds 15% of quality formula. Real user access should immediately reflect in quality score. Internal access (brain_replay/dream) already passes internal=True to avoid inflating access_count, and should similarly not trigger quality recalc

memories.content: When closing quality pipeline gaps in background/internal operations, wrap all QualityScoreCalculator.recalculate_single_memory_quality() calls in try/except with logger.warning. These operations (consolidation, reconsolidation, merge) should never fail the parent operation due to a quality scoring error — the quality score is supplementary metadata, not critical data. Use lazy imports (from .quality_tracking import ...) inside the try block to avoid circular imports since these modules don't normally depend on quality_tracking. Pattern: (1) identify operations that modify quality formula inputs via set_payload or direct upsert, (2) add recalc after the payload write, (3) wrap in try/except, (4) gate on conditions (e.g., internal=False for reconsolidation).

Added quality recalculation to _sync_relation_to_qdrant() in graph.py after the set_payload that updates the relations list. This is the single choke point for ALL relationship creation paths — inference, session consolidation, reconsolidation co-access, and direct create_relationship calls all go through this function. Used logger.debug (not warning) since this runs frequently during batch inference operations.
memories.decision: Add quality recalc to _sync_relation_to_qdrant at the graph.py level rather than individual callers
memories.rationale: Single insertion point covers all graph paths at once — inference (relationship_inference.py), session consolidation (session_extraction.py), co-access linking (reconsolidation.py), and direct API calls. Relations are 10% of quality formula weight.

memories.content: Added content sanitization (clean_content + normalize_tags) and quality recalculation to the audit restore_to_version() path in audit.py. Audit snapshots may contain pre-sanitization data from before the enrichment pipeline was added, so restoring them could inject dirty data. The sanitization runs as a secondary set_payload after the main restore, then quality is recalculated.
memories.decision: Sanitize restored values and recalculate quality in audit.py restore_to_version
memories.rationale: Audit snapshots (old_values) capture data at write time — snapshots created before the clean_content pipeline was added contain unsanitized data. The two-step approach (restore raw, then sanitize) ensures the audit log captures what was actually restored while the final state is clean.

memories.content: Added normalize_tags() to both consolidation paths: merge_with_existing (line 115, dedup merge) and consolidate_cluster (line 454, cluster consolidation). Previously both merged tags via set operations (list(set(...))) which doesn't lowercase, deduplicate after lowering, or remove short tags. The quality recalc was already added in a prior session but the tags fed to it were dirty.
memories.decision: Add normalize_tags to consolidation merge and cluster tag aggregation
memories.rationale: Tags from different memories being merged may have inconsistent casing (e.g., 'Python' vs 'python'), near-duplicates that only differ by case, or very short tags. normalize_tags handles lowercase, dedup, and min-length filtering.

memories.content: Added clean_content and normalize_tags sanitization to the version restore endpoint in routers/memories.py (line 998-1000). Version snapshots capture content and tags at snapshot time — snapshots created before the enrichment pipeline was added could contain dirty whitespace or unnormalized tags. Quality recalc was already present at line 1022.
memories.decision: Sanitize content and tags during version restore before writing to Qdrant
memories.rationale: Version snapshots are immutable historical records. Restoring from an old snapshot could reintroduce dirty data that was created before clean_content/normalize_tags was added to the store pipeline. Sanitizing at restore time ensures the active memory is always clean.

memories.content: The MemoryUpdate Pydantic model does NOT include a 'type' field, which means type changes via PATCH are structurally impossible — Pydantic silently drops the 'type' key from update_data. Type-change validation code in update_memory is defensive but will never trigger in the current schema. This is actually a good design: memory type is an immutable characteristic set at creation time. If type changes are ever needed, the MemoryUpdate model would need to be extended first.

When using agent teams for multi-file surgical edits with a detailed plan, the pattern is: (1) Create team, (2) Create all tasks with detailed file:line instructions and exact code snippets, (3) Spawn all agents in parallel with bypassPermissions mode, (4) Wait for task completion via TaskList polling, (5) Verify all diffs, (6) Shut down agents and delete team. Agents may add bonus improvements beyond the spec — review diffs carefully. Router-fixer added 409 conflict check and quality recalc to rate_memory endpoint, which were valid additions. Total time for 5 parallel agents across 5 files was ~2-3 minutes vs serial would have been ~5-8 minutes.

Made the Intelligence & Analytics settings (audit retention days, pattern detection interval, quality update interval) editable from the dashboard Settings page. Previously these were disabled/hardcoded with 'Configure in backend' text. Now they are controlled inputs bound to React state, saved via POST /settings, and applied at runtime via _apply_intelligence_settings() which mutates MemoryLifecycleManager.PURGE_RETENTION_DAYS and reschedules APScheduler jobs. On restart, scheduler.py and lifecycle.py load persisted values from settings.json.

To make APScheduler job intervals editable at runtime: (1) Add settings to settings.json via existing POST /settings flow, (2) In the POST handler, call job.reschedule(trigger=IntervalTrigger(hours=N)) after writing the file, (3) In scheduler.py get_scheduler(), load settings.json at init time and use the persisted values for initial add_job() calls. This ensures both runtime changes and restart persistence. The _reschedule_job() helper wraps the reschedule in try/except with logging since the scheduler may not be enabled. Validation (clamp to min/max) happens in _apply_intelligence_settings() before calling reschedule.

For targeted multi-file changes with a detailed plan (~80 lines across 4 files: Settings.tsx, admin.py, scheduler.py, lifecycle.py), direct implementation by the lead agent took about 3 minutes with 10 sequential edits. This confirms the earlier learning that agent teams add overhead for small surgical edits. The changes touched: (1) TypeScript interface + defaults + JSX card replacement, (2) Python default dict + helper functions + POST handler hook, (3) Python settings loader + variable substitution in job creation, (4) Python settings loader + class attribute initialization.

MemoryDetailPanel Related section was rendering blank content and no relationship types because of field name mismatches between the graph API response and the frontend component. The graph API get_related_memories() returns {id, type, preview, distance, relationship_path} but the component read {content, relations[0].relation_type}.
memories.error_message: Related memories section showed only type badges with no content text or relationship labels — fields were undefined due to API/component field name mismatch
memories.solution: Changed component to read rel.preview (not rel.content), rel.relationship_path[0] (not rel.relations[0].relation_type), and added fallback text. Also added distance indicator for multi-hop relationships.

memories.content: Anomaly detection in insights.py was flagging brand-new memories as 'orphaned' and 'high_importance_low_access' because both checks had no minimum age requirement. New memories naturally have zero relations (inference hasn't run yet) and zero accesses (nobody has searched for them yet), so they always triggered both anomaly types.
memories.error_message: Anomaly detection false positives: all new high-quality memories flagged as high_importance_low_access and orphaned immediately after creation
memories.solution: Added minimum age gates to both anomaly checks: orphaned requires age_days >= 3 (inference needs time), high_importance_low_access requires age_days >= 7 (access needs time to accumulate). Moved created_at/age_days computation above the orphan check since it was previously computed after.

memories.content: Centralized safe_set_payload() wrapper pattern for Qdrant payload updates: Create a single function that (1) applies client.set_payload(), (2) checks if any quality-affecting fields were modified using a QUALITY_AFFECTING_FIELDS frozenset, (3) auto-triggers QualityScoreCalculator.recalculate_single_memory_quality() if quality fields changed, (4) optionally runs post-update enrichment pipeline, (5) wraps quality recalc in try/except so it never fails the parent operation. Use recalc_quality=False for high-frequency operations (access tracking) and archived memories. This single wrapper closes 11+ quality pipeline gaps across the codebase by replacing raw client.set_payload() calls.
Added resolved_at timestamp field to Memory model and mark_resolved() function to track when errors are resolved, enabling time-to-resolution metrics and recently-resolved filtering.
memories.decision: Add resolved_at: Optional[str] = None to Memory model, set it in mark_resolved() via datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
memories.rationale: Without a resolution timestamp, the system could only tell IF an error was resolved but not WHEN, making it impossible to calculate time-to-resolution metrics or filter for recently resolved errors.

memories.content: When using agent teams for parallel file edits, assign one file per agent to avoid write conflicts. The centralized wrapper pattern works well with teams: lead creates the shared function first (blocking dependency), then spawns agents in parallel to replace call sites in their assigned files. With 3 agents working on 4 files simultaneously, total time was ~3 minutes vs ~8 minutes serial.

Update sanitization must cover ALL text fields, not just content and tags. When updating memories via PATCH, apply clean_content() to solution, prevention, rationale, decision, context, and error_message fields — not just content. Also validate type-change requirements comprehensively: changing to 'error' requires error_message + solution + prevention (not just the first two).

Decomposed the monolithic /memory-audit command (230 lines, 3 phases, 13 mutation steps) into 7 focused commands: memory-search, memory-export, memory-resolve, memory-graph, memory-cleanup, memory-consolidate, and a rewritten read-only memory-audit. Each command uses YAML frontmatter with description, allowed-tools, and model: sonnet. The rewritten memory-audit is now diagnostics-only (118 lines) with recommendations pointing to the focused commands.

When decomposing a monolithic slash command into focused commands, follow this pattern: (1) Identify read-only vs mutation operations, (2) Group mutations by domain (errors→resolve, graph→graph, cleanup→cleanup, consolidation→consolidate), (3) Make the original command read-only diagnostics that recommends the focused commands, (4) Each command gets its own allowed-tools list scoped to only the MCP tools it needs, (5) Use model: sonnet for all commands to save cost on procedural workflows, (6) Keep each command self-contained with clear step numbering and summary output format. This pattern preserves all functionality while enabling targeted execution.

Claude Code slash commands in ~/.claude/commands/ register immediately after file creation — no restart needed. The skill list in system reminders updates on the next tool call. YAML frontmatter fields: description (shown in skill list), allowed-tools (array of tool patterns with wildcards like mcp__memory__*), model (sonnet/opus/haiku). The $ARGUMENTS variable captures user input after the command name.

Qdrant's client.scroll() offset parameter is a point ID (cursor-based), NOT an integer offset. Passing offset=50 does NOT skip 50 records — it looks for a point with ID 50. For proper integer offset pagination, use client.query_points() with OrderByQuery and the offset parameter, which supports true integer offsets. Example: client.query_points(collection_name=col, query=models.OrderByQuery(order_by=models.OrderBy(key='created_at', direction='desc')), query_filter=filter, limit=50, offset=50).

Backend paginated response pattern for Qdrant-backed APIs: (1) Define PaginatedResponse Pydantic model with items, total, limit, offset fields. (2) Use client.count(collection_name, count_filter, exact=True) with the SAME filter to get total. (3) Use client.query_points() with OrderByQuery for proper integer offset pagination instead of client.scroll(). (4) Return PaginatedResponse(items=memories, total=count_result.count, limit=limit, offset=offset). Frontend extracts data.items and data.total, uses total for page count and Next button disable logic: disabled={(page+1) >= Math.ceil(total/limit)}.

Changed GET /memories from returning list[Memory] to PaginatedMemories{items, total, limit, offset} and switched from client.scroll() to client.query_points() with OrderByQuery for proper integer offset pagination. Added archived=False filter to exclude archived memories by default.

QR Scanner modal on PilotViewer page would not return/close after successful scan. The handleScannerSuccess callback suffered from stale closure issues due to React Query mutation objects (doMarkArrived) not being referentially stable across renders, causing the callback to hold stale references.
memories.error_message: QR scanner modal stays open after successful scan - does not return to pilot page
memories.solution: Used useRef pattern: added scannerBookingRef alongside scannerBooking state. handleScannerSuccess reads from ref instead of state. Also added a 2-second safety fallback useEffect in QRScannerModal that auto-closes if stuck on success screen. Key insight: doMarkArrived depends on markArrivedMutation which recreates every render, so any callback depending on it gets recreated too.

memories.content: Duplicate WhatsApp confirmation messages sent when creating a booking. Two independent paths both called the same /ticket/send-confirmation endpoint: (1) Frontend bookingService.ts createBooking() called sendBookingConfirmation() fire-and-forget, (2) DB trigger trigger_send_booking_confirmation on lead_bookings INSERT fired pg_notify which confirmation-listener/index.js picked up and called the same endpoint.
memories.error_message: Duplicate WhatsApp messages sent on booking creation - one from frontend, one from DB trigger
memories.solution: Removed the sendBookingConfirmation() call from createBooking() in bookingService.ts (lines 145-150). The DB trigger + confirmation-listener is the single source of truth for automatic confirmations. The manual resend button in BookingForm.tsx still works independently.

memories.content: In React, useCallback dependency arrays are evaluated at render time, not call time. If function A depends on function B but B is declared after A (using const), adding B to A's dependency array causes a TDZ (Temporal Dead Zone) ReferenceError at render time. The workaround is to use an empty dependency array with eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps, or reorder the declarations so dependencies come first.

For the duplicate WhatsApp confirmation bug, chose to remove the frontend sendBookingConfirmation() call from createBooking() rather than removing the DB trigger. The DB trigger + pg_notify + confirmation-listener is the proper architectural path for automatic notifications.
memories.decision: Keep DB trigger as single source of truth for automatic WhatsApp confirmations, remove frontend fire-and-forget call
memories.rationale: DB triggers guarantee execution regardless of which client creates the booking (frontend, API, admin tool). The frontend call was redundant and created a race condition. The manual resend button remains available for cases where the automatic message fails.

memories.content: Deployment pattern for compta frontend: (1) npm run build in local frontend/ dir, (2) rsync --delete dist/ to h4ckm1n@terralao.la:/home/h4ckm1n/Enduro/compta/frontend/dist/, (3) docker restart compta-frontend. The frontend dist is volume-mounted into the nginx container, so no Docker rebuild needed. For DB migrations: ssh + docker exec -i compta-db psql -U compta_user -d compta_db < migration.sql. Remote repo path is /home/h4ckm1n/Enduro/compta/ (NOT /opt/compta/).

Split claude-mem-service monolith into 3 services: claude-mem-api (FastAPI, SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false), claude-mem-worker (scheduler only, health on port 8101), claude-mem-frontend (Nginx + React SPA on host port 8100). Qdrant and Neo4j unchanged. Nginx reverse-proxies API routes and WebSocket to the API container, serves static frontend files directly. MCP server still calls localhost:8100 with no changes needed.

Microservice split pattern for Docker monoliths: (1) Create shared backend Dockerfile without frontend build stage, (2) Create frontend Dockerfile with Nginx that reverse-proxies API routes and serves SPA with try_files fallback, (3) Create worker.py standalone entrypoint that inits same collections, starts scheduler, runs minimal health HTTP server on separate port, blocks on shutdown event, (4) Use YAML anchor x-backend-env for shared DB connection vars in docker-compose, (5) docker-compose.override.yml disables Nginx frontend via profiles=['production'], exposes API directly on host port, adds Vite dev server with HMR, (6) Production: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml up -d, Dev: docker compose up -d (auto-merges override), (7) Keep original Dockerfile for rollback safety.

After splitting a Docker Compose monolith into multiple services, orphan containers from the old service name (e.g., claude-mem-service) may still hold the host port. Use 'docker rm -f <old-container>' or '--remove-orphans' flag on docker compose up to clear them. Also, when the old and new services share the same compose project name, Docker may warn about orphans but won't auto-remove them.

Claude Brain memory system now runs as 5 Docker containers: claude-mem-qdrant (vector DB, ports 6333-6334), claude-mem-neo4j (graph DB, ports 7474/7687), claude-mem-api (FastAPI on internal port 8100, scheduler disabled), claude-mem-worker (scheduler + health on internal port 8101), claude-mem-frontend (Nginx on host port 8100, proxies to API). Key files: docker/backend.Dockerfile, docker/frontend.Dockerfile, docker/nginx.conf, src/worker.py. Production: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml up -d. Dev mode with Vite HMR: docker compose up -d (uses override). Original monolith Dockerfile kept for rollback.

Decomposed the Claude Brain API monolith into 8 focused microservices: Core (CRUD + WebSocket, port 8100), Embeddings (ML models, port 8102), Search (semantic/keyword/hybrid, port 8103), Graph (Neo4j, port 8104), Brain (replay/dream/inference, port 8105), Quality (scoring/lifecycle, port 8106), Analytics (trends/insights, port 8107), Admin (settings/export/sessions/documents/temporal/audit, port 8108). Total: 12 containers (8 backend + frontend + worker + qdrant + neo4j). All share the same backend Docker image except Embeddings which has its own Dockerfile with ML models.

Microservice factory pattern for FastAPI services: Create a shared base.py with create_app(title, routers, init_qdrant, init_docs) factory function that handles lifespan (Qdrant/docs init, embedding validation, graph cleanup), CORS, GZip middleware, and a /health endpoint for Docker health checks. Each service is a ~20-line file that imports its routers and calls create_app(). Services run via 'python -m src.services.<name>_app' with if __name__ == '__main__': uvicorn.run(...) blocks. The shared base ensures consistent middleware and health checking across all services. CRITICAL: Always include a /health endpoint in the factory — Docker health checks need it.

Embedding service HTTP client pattern: Create embedding_client.py as a dual-mode module that checks EMBEDDING_SERVICE_URL env var. If set, routes all embed/rerank calls via httpx.Client (with connection pooling and 60s timeout) to the standalone embedding service. If not set, loads models locally (backward compat). Then modify embeddings.py and reranker.py to delegate to embedding_client — embeddings.py re-exports functions from embedding_client, reranker.py extracts text content from complex objects and delegates scoring to embedding_client.rerank_texts(). The embedding_app.py is standalone FastAPI that loads models on startup via lifespan. Key endpoints: POST /embed (document prefix), POST /embed_query (query prefix), POST /embed_batch, POST /rerank, GET /health, GET /config.

Docker health check failed with 404 on microservice containers because the base.py factory function did not include a /health endpoint. Only the admin service was healthy because its admin router already had /health. All other domain services (core, search, graph, brain, quality, analytics) returned 404 for health checks.
memories.error_message: GET /health HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found — docker compose reports container as unhealthy
memories.solution: Added @app.get('/health') endpoint directly in the create_app() factory function in base.py, so every service automatically gets a /health route. Returns {status: 'ok', service: title}.

memories.content: Port mismatch in embedding.Dockerfile — EXPOSE and CMD used port 8101 but docker-compose.yml health check and EMBEDDING_SERVICE_URL referenced port 8102. The embedding service started on 8101 inside the container but other services tried to reach it on 8102.
memories.error_message: Connection refused on port 8102 — embedding service listening on 8101
memories.solution: Fixed EXPOSE 8101 to EXPOSE 8102 and CMD port argument from 8101 to 8102 in docker/embedding.Dockerfile.

memories.content: The embedding.Dockerfile needs COPY src/__init__.py ./src/__init__.py in addition to COPY src/services/ ./src/services/ because Python's module system requires __init__.py files in parent packages. Without it, 'python -m src.services.embedding_app' fails with ModuleNotFoundError because 'src' is not recognized as a package.

After microservice decomposition, scheduler job trigger endpoints returned 404 because the admin service has SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false while the actual APScheduler runs only in the worker process. Nginx was routing /scheduler/* to admin instead of worker.
memories.error_message: POST /scheduler/jobs/memory_strength_update_job/trigger → 404 Not Found (detail: Job not found or scheduler disabled)
memories.solution: Added scheduler HTTP endpoints (GET /scheduler/status, POST /scheduler/jobs/{id}/trigger, POST /scheduler/trigger-all) to worker.py HealthHandler. Updated nginx.conf to add worker upstream and route /scheduler and /jobs to worker instead of admin. Removed scheduler|jobs from admin catch-all regex.

memories.content: After microservice decomposition, Nginx regex location ^/(brain|inference) caught requests for /brain.svg static file and routed them to the brain backend service, returning 404 instead of serving the SVG from the SPA.
memories.error_message: GET /brain.svg → 404 Not Found (routed to brain service instead of static files)
memories.solution: Added a root-level static file location block with regex before API routes: location ~* ^/[^/]+\.(svg|png|ico|json|txt|webmanifest)$ { root /usr/share/nginx/html; try_files $uri =404; } — this has higher priority than the API regex routes.

memories.content: Microservice decomposition Nginx routing pattern: Use location priority order to prevent conflicts. Order: (1) Exact matches (location =) for overlapping paths like /memories/search, (2) Static file regex for root-level assets before API routes, (3) API regex routes per service, (4) Worker/scheduler routes before admin catch-all, (5) WebSocket upgrade, (6) Static /assets with cache headers, (7) SPA fallback (try_files $uri /index.html). Always test with curl -sv to see which upstream handles each request.

Route scheduler endpoints to the worker process (port 8101) instead of admin service (port 8108) in the microservice architecture. The worker is the only process running APScheduler, so it must own the scheduler API.
memories.decision: Scheduler HTTP endpoints live on the worker process HealthHandler, routed via Nginx upstream worker
memories.rationale: APScheduler state is process-local. The admin service runs with SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false and has no access to job state. The worker already had a health check HTTP server on port 8101 — extending it with scheduler management endpoints was the least-effort solution.

memories.content: Nginx SPA + Microservice API coexistence pattern: When SPA page routes overlap with API route prefixes (e.g., /analytics is both a React Router page and an API prefix), use an Nginx map on the Accept header to distinguish browser navigation from API calls. Browser sends Accept: text/html; axios/fetch sends Accept: application/json. Add `map $http_accept $is_spa_navigation { ~text/html 1; default 0; }` at http context level, then add `if ($is_spa_navigation) { rewrite ^ /index.html last; }` inside each API location block. The `rewrite ... last` re-enters location matching and lands on the SPA fallback location which serves index.html. This is a documented safe use of if in Nginx (rewrite with last flag). No code changes needed in frontend or backend — purely Nginx config.

Created setup.sh at ~/.claude/memory/setup.sh — a one-command installer for the Claude Brain Memory System. 674 lines, idempotent, cross-platform (macOS + Linux). 9-step flow: prerequisites check, repo clone/update, env setup, Docker build, container start with phased health checks, MCP server npm install, MCP registration in ~/.claude.json via python3 with env vars, CRUD verification, summary banner. Uses --remove-orphans to clean monolith-era containers.

Safe Python inline scripting in bash: Never interpolate shell variables directly into Python string literals (e.g., python3 -c "open('$VAR')") — this creates command injection risk if paths contain quotes. Instead, pass values via environment variables: MYVAR="$shell_var" python3 -c "import os; path = os.environ['MYVAR']". This is safe against all special characters in file paths and works on both macOS and Linux without extra dependencies.

Bash temporary directory safety pattern: Use mktemp -d instead of /tmp/name-$$ for temporary directories. Wrap with trap for cleanup on exit: tmpdir=$(mktemp -d) || die; trap "rm -rf '$tmpdir'" EXIT. After successful use, rm -rf and clear the trap with trap - EXIT. The mktemp approach avoids PID prediction attacks and handles cleanup even if the script fails partway through due to set -e.

Created install.sh bootstrap script at ~/.claude/memory/install.sh for curl-pipe-bash installation. Usage: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/h4ckm1n-dev/Claude-Brain/main/memory/install.sh | bash. The bootstrap handles repo clone/update (with rsync fallback for non-git ~/.claude dirs), then exec's setup.sh in a new bash process. Key detail: uses exec bash to avoid running from piped stdin. Also patched setup.sh to detect non-interactive mode via [[ -t 0 ]] — auto-installs Docker on Linux when piped, prompts when interactive.

Booking confirmation in ticket.py now logs outgoing Message to SQLite and calls mark_customer_responded() after successful WhatsApp send. This triggers human takeover when customer replies. Imports from app.main are done inside the try block to avoid circular imports (main.py imports ticket router at module level).

Remote deployment for WhatsApp bot: rsync to /home/h4ckm1n/Enduro/compta/Whatsapps/ (NOT /home/h4ckm1n/Enduro/Whatsapps/). The docker-compose.yml is in /home/h4ckm1n/Enduro/compta/ and volume-mounts ./Whatsapps/app:/app/app, so the compta/Whatsapps path is what the container uses. The standalone /home/h4ckm1n/Enduro/Whatsapps/ is an older copy not used by Docker. After rsync, restart with: docker restart compta-whatsapp (no rebuild needed since app/ is volume-mounted).

Voice2type architecture: 8-crate Cargo workspace (v2t-core, v2t-audio, v2t-vad, v2t-whisper, v2t-models, v2t-pipeline, v2t-claude, v2t-app). Two-stage whisper pipeline for wake word detection: Silero VAD gates audio, whisper-tiny transcribes short segments for 'Ok Bro' regex match, then whisper-large-v3-turbo transcribes full command. 4 threads: main (tao event loop + tray-icon), audio (cpal callback + ringbuf), processing (resample + VAD), inference (whisper + claude CLI). Channels: lock-free ring buffer for audio, crossbeam bounded channels for segments and events.

Voice2type project environment: Rust 1.88.0, macOS Darwin 25.2.0, Apple M4 Pro, 48GB RAM. Claude Code CLI v2.1.38 at /Users/h4ckm1n/.local/bin/claude. Built-in MacBook Pro microphone at 44.1kHz (1 channel). Project directory: /Users/h4ckm1n/Documents/SabaiDev/Voice2type/. Key crates: whisper-rs 0.15.1 (Codeberg), cpal 0.15, rubato 0.16, voice_activity_detector 0.4 (Silero V5), tray-icon 0.19, tao 0.31, hf-hub 0.4, crossbeam-channel 0.5, arboard 3. Models: ggml-tiny.bin (75MB) for wake word, ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin (1.5GB) for transcription, from ggerganov/whisper.cpp on HuggingFace.

Two-stage whisper wake word detection pattern: Stage 1 (always-on) - Silero VAD detects speech onset, accumulate up to 3 seconds of audio, transcribe with whisper-tiny (~50ms), regex match against wake phrase pattern /(?i)\b(ok(?:ay)?)\s*,?\s*(bro)\b/. Stage 2 (on match) - Continue recording while VAD detects speech, end on 1.5s silence or 30s max, transcribe with whisper-large-v3-turbo (~300ms for 10s audio), send to Claude CLI. State machine: IDLE -> LISTENING -> TRANSCRIBING_WAKE -> CHECK_WAKE -> RECORDING_COMMAND -> TRANSCRIBING_COMMAND -> SEND_TO_CLAUDE -> IDLE. Audio pipeline: cpal 44.1kHz capture -> ringbuf lock-free -> rubato resample to 16kHz -> Silero VAD 512-sample chunks -> crossbeam channel to inference thread.

Build sequence for Voice2type: Phase 1 (Week 1) - v2t-core (types, config, errors) then v2t-audio (cpal capture, rubato resample, ringbuf). Phase 2 (Week 2) - v2t-vad (Silero wrapper), v2t-models (hf-hub download), v2t-whisper (whisper-rs inference + wake word regex). Phase 3 (Week 3) - v2t-claude (CLI invocation + clipboard), v2t-pipeline (state machine coordinator). Phase 4 (Week 4) - v2t-app (tao event loop, tray-icon, macOS .app bundle with Info.plist). Each crate testable in isolation before integration.

Voice2Type is a Rust macOS menubar app with 8 crates: v2t-core (types/config), v2t-audio (cpal+rubato+ringbuf), v2t-vad (Silero VAD v0.2), v2t-whisper (whisper-rs v0.15), v2t-models (hf-hub), v2t-claude (CLI+clipboard), v2t-pipeline (state machine+threads), v2t-app (tao+tray-icon). Workspace at /Users/h4ckm1n/Documents/SabaiDev/Voice2type/. Uses wake word 'Ok Bro' via regex, two-stage whisper pipeline (tiny for wake word, turbo for commands), and sends to `claude -p`.

Used tao v0.34 EventLoopBuilder::with_user_event().build() pattern for macOS event loop, NOT EventLoop::with_user_event() which doesn't exist. tao event_loop.run() returns ! (never), so main() cannot return Result - use separate setup function with expect() instead.
Crate version corrections from plan: voice_activity_detector v0.2 (not v0.4), rubato v1 (not v0.16), tao v0.34 (not v0.31), tray-icon v0.21 (not v0.19). Edition 2021 (not 2024 which doesn't exist).

For sharing event callbacks across threads in Rust, use Arc<dyn Fn(Event) + Send + Sync>. The set_state() helper function must accept &Arc<dyn Fn(...)> not &dyn Fn(...), because Arc<dyn Fn> does not implement Fn directly - you need to dereference through the Arc. Pattern: fn helper(state: &AtomicU8, new_state: State, cb: &Arc<dyn Fn(Event) + Send + Sync>) { state.store(...); cb(Event::StateChanged(new_state)); }

rubato v1.x uses the Adapter trait for audio buffers, with Async::new_sinc() for resampling. Key API: Async::<f32>::new_sinc(ratio, max_relative_ratio, &params, chunk_size, channels, FixedAsync::Input). Process with process(&adapter, 0, None). The MonoSlice adapter pattern wraps &[f32] as single-channel audio.

Upgraded v2t-app menubar from minimal 2-item tray (Pause/Quit) to full macOS menubar app with status display, language/model/response-action submenus with CheckMenuItem radio groups, Open Config, About dialog, and keyboard accelerators. All config fields from v2t-core are now exposed in the UI.

In tray-icon 0.21 (which re-exports muda 0.17), the Accelerator struct is NOT directly re-exported from tray_icon::menu. It lives in tray_icon::menu::accelerator::Accelerator submodule. Use `use tray_icon::menu::accelerator::Accelerator;` not `use tray_icon::menu::Accelerator;`. Parse accelerators from strings like "CmdOrCtrl+P".parse::<Accelerator>().ok().

For pipeline restart in v2t-app: lock the Arc<Mutex<Pipeline>> to stop the old pipeline (which joins threads), release the lock, create a new Pipeline with updated config and fresh EventLoopProxy clone, then lock again to replace. Two separate lock/unlock cycles avoid holding the mutex while constructing the new pipeline. The restart_pipeline() helper function takes &Arc<Mutex<Pipeline>>, &AppConfig, and &EventLoopProxy<AppEvent>.

Rebranded Voice2Type to OkBro. The wake word 'Ok Bro' becomes the app identity. Changed all user-facing strings: menu items, About dialog, tooltips, log messages, Info.plist (CFBundleName, CFBundleDisplayName, CFBundleIdentifier → dev.sabai.okbro), bundle script (APP_NAME, BUNDLE_ID). Internal crate names (v2t-core, v2t-app, etc.) kept as-is — only user-facing branding changed.

OkBro (Voice2type) app crashed on launch with panic: 'Failed to download command model: Model("Download failed for ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin: Lock acquisition failed")'. The hf-hub crate uses file-based locks in the HuggingFace blob cache directory. If a previous download is interrupted (Ctrl+C, crash), stale .lock files remain and block subsequent downloads.
memories.error_message: Failed to download command model: Model("Download failed for ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin: Lock acquisition failed: ...lock")
memories.solution: Remove stale .lock files from ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--ggerganov--whisper.cpp/blobs/*.lock. Also check for incomplete .part files — if the download was interrupted, the .part file may need time to complete on next run. The symlink directory ~/.cache/voice2type/models/ is created fresh by ModelManager::ensure_model().

memories.content: Added a PostToolUse hook (context7-docs-capture.sh) that automatically stores Context7 library documentation into the memory system as docs-type memories. Triggers on mcp__context7__get-library-docs tool calls. Deduplicates by checking existing docs memories for the same library ID + topic combo. Stores with source=context7://{libraryID}, truncated to 8000 chars, tagged with library name, org, topic, and context7. Registered in settings.json PostToolUse array with async:true.

Replaced the tray menu Language/Model/Response submenus with a wry WebView settings window in v2t-app. Menu now has: Status (grey), Pause/Resume, Settings..., About, Quit. Settings window uses HTML/CSS/JS with macOS-native styling (system font, dark mode, rounded cards). IPC flow: Rust serializes AppConfig to JSON -> embedded in HTML -> JS form -> window.ipc.postMessage(JSON) -> Rust ipc_handler deserializes and saves.

In tao v0.34, to hide the dock icon on macOS (show only menubar tray icon), use EventLoopExtMacOS trait (not EventLoopBuilderExtMacOS which doesn't exist). Call set_activation_policy(ActivationPolicy::Accessory) on the EventLoop after building it, not on the builder. Import: use tao::platform::macos::{ActivationPolicy, EventLoopExtMacOS};

wry WebView settings window pattern for tao menubar apps: Store settings window as Option<(Window, WebView)> in the event loop closure. On open: check if Some -> focus existing window, else create WindowBuilder + WebViewBuilder with_html() and with_ipc_handler(). IPC handler forwards messages via EventLoopProxy. On save: deserialize JSON from IPC into config struct, save to disk, close window (set to None), restart pipeline. Handle WindowEvent::CloseRequested to clean up. Cancel button sends sentinel string '__cancel__' via IPC.

Context7 docs capture PostToolUse hook was silently failing because it used wrong field names for the Claude Code hook input JSON. The hook read .input and .output but Claude Code PostToolUse hooks provide .tool_input and .tool_response (array of {type, text} objects).
memories.error_message: Hook silently exiting with empty LIBRARY_ID — jq path .input.context7CompatibleLibraryID returned empty because the correct path is .tool_input.context7CompatibleLibraryID
memories.solution: Changed field paths in context7-docs-capture.sh: .input -> .tool_input, .output -> .tool_response[0].text (using jq expression: [.tool_response[]? | .text // empty] | join for multi-response support)

memories.content: Audio pipeline dropping 99% of samples due to ring buffer read + resampler interaction bug. capture.read_samples() consumed samples from the SPSC ring buffer via pop_slice(), but when fewer than resampler.input_frames_next() samples were available, those consumed samples were discarded on `continue`. Result: only ~1100 out of ~80000 expected samples per 5 seconds reached VAD, causing wake word detection to never trigger.
memories.error_message: VAD never detects SpeechStart — pipeline stays idle. Whisper reports 'input is too short - 40 ms < 100 ms' when it occasionally fires.
memories.solution: Added an accumulation buffer (Vec<f32>) between ring buffer reads and resampler. Samples are appended to accum_buf on each read, and only drained when accum_buf.len() >= resampler.input_frames_next(). This preserves all partial reads until a full resampler chunk is available.

memories.content: Whisper-tiny auto-detects language as French for a French-speaking user, transcribing the English wake word "ok bro" as "Ok, bon" or other French phrases. The wake word regex never matches because it expects English text containing "ok/okay/oké bro".
memories.error_message: Wake word never detected - whisper transcribes "ok bro" as French text like "Ok, bon. Toi tu me feront un résumé."
memories.solution: Force English language for wake word model: params.set_language(Some("en")) when model == ModelType::WakeWord. Keep auto-detect or user-configured language for the command model only.

memories.content: Auto-send flight certificates via WhatsApp when pilot marks a flight as completed on PilotViewer page. Implemented as frontend-only fire-and-forget in handleMarkCompleted callback. After markCompletedMutation succeeds, sendCertificateAfterCompletion runs without await, loading the active template (cached in useRef for the session), building the request via bookingToCertificateRequest, sending via sendCertificates (3x retry + 15s timeout), and marking certificate_sent_at via markCertificateSent. Guards skip silently for: no phone, no participants, no template, already sent.

Template caching pattern for fire-and-forget operations in React: Use two useRef flags — one for the cached data (cachedTemplateRef) and one boolean for whether load was attempted (templateLoadedRef). On first call, set loaded=true and fetch. If fetch returns null, reset loaded=false to allow retry on next invocation. This avoids repeated API calls while still recovering from temporary failures (like template not yet configured). Used in PilotViewer.tsx for certificate template caching across multiple flight completions in a single session.

Added project name normalization to the memory enrichment pipeline. normalize_project() maps known aliases to canonical slugs (e.g., 'Claude Brain Memory System' → 'claude-brain') and normalizes unknown projects to lowercase-hyphenated format. Inserted at step 2 in enhance_and_validate() between clean_content and auto_enrich_fields.

Project name normalization pattern for memory systems: maintain a PROJECT_ALIASES dict mapping known variants to canonical slugs. For unknown projects, apply lowercase + spaces/underscores to hyphens normalization. Insert normalization early in the enrichment pipeline (before field derivation) so all downstream processing uses the canonical name. Also document canonical names in CLAUDE.md so the AI agent uses correct names from the start, reducing normalization load.

The enhance_and_validate() pipeline in memories.py now has 8 steps: (1) clean_content, (2) normalize_project, (3) auto_enrich_fields, (4) auto_enrich_tags, (5) semantic dedup, (6) quality validation, (7) legacy content filters, (8) auto-captured boilerplate rejection. This pipeline runs for both single and bulk memory creation.

nginx was routing /jobs/prune and /jobs/tag to the worker service (port 8101) instead of the admin service (port 8108), causing 404 errors on the dashboard Settings page when clicking Prune or Tag buttons.
memories.error_message: POST /jobs/prune 404 Not Found — nginx routed to worker upstream instead of admin
memories.solution: Moved /jobs from the worker location block to the admin location block in docker/nginx.conf. Split the regex from ^/(scheduler|jobs) into separate ^/scheduler (worker) and added jobs to the admin service pattern.

memories.content: After editing nginx.conf on the host, the running container still had the old config because the file is baked into the Docker image via frontend.Dockerfile COPY, not volume-mounted. Running nginx -s reload inside the container had no effect.
memories.error_message: Container still has old nginx config after host file edit — config is baked into image, not volume-mounted
memories.solution: Rebuild the frontend Docker image with docker compose -f docker-compose.yml build claude-mem-frontend, then recreate the container with docker compose up -d claude-mem-frontend.

memories.content: docker-compose.override.yml changes the deployment topology: disables nginx frontend (profiles: production), exposes core directly on port 8100, and starts Vite dev server on 5173. Running docker compose up -d uses dev mode. Production mode requires: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml up -d.

Vite dev proxy config in vite.config.ts referenced non-existent claude-mem-api:8100 service. In the microservice architecture, each service has its own container name and port: core:8100, worker:8101, embeddings:8102, search:8103, graph:8104, brain:8105, quality:8106, analytics:8107, admin:8108. Updated proxy to route each path to the correct service.

Removed Consolidation page and Temporal page from the frontend dashboard. Consolidation functionality is already available in the Settings page. Temporal page was unused. Deleted 4 files: pages/Consolidation.tsx, pages/Temporal.tsx, api/temporal.ts, hooks/useTemporal.ts. Updated App.tsx routes, Sidebar.tsx navigation, and QuickActions.tsx.

Session-start memories were rejected by two quality gates: (1) quality.py boilerplate detector penalized -0.40 for content matching 'session started for project' when tagged session-start/auto-captured, pushing score below 0.55 threshold; (2) memories.py step 8 boilerplate filter rejected auto-captured content starting with 'session started for project'. Both gates prevented sessions from appearing on the Sessions page.
memories.error_message: Memory quality too low (score 0.45) — auto-captured boilerplate detected for session-start memories
memories.solution: Exempted session lifecycle memories (tagged session-start or session-end) from both boilerplate penalties: quality.py checks is_session_lifecycle before applying -0.40 penalty, memories.py step 8 checks is_session_lifecycle before rejecting.

memories.content: Session lifecycle tracking pattern: SessionStart hook creates a session via POST /sessions/new, stores a context memory with session_id and tags=[session-start, auto-captured], then exports MEMORY_SESSION_ID to CLAUDE_ENV_FILE. The Sessions page discovers sessions by scanning all memories with non-null session_id field, grouping by session, and deriving the project name from the most common project across that session's memories. Session-start/session-end memories must be exempted from boilerplate quality penalties to allow this flow.
